examples.solution_text:
a. One application uses the full baseline width.

$\begin{align*} A &\approx \frac{27}{2}(20.8+29.2)\\ &\approx 675\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$

b. Each strip has width $h=27\div2=13.5\text{ m}$.

$\begin{align*} A &\approx A_1+A_2\\ &\approx \frac{13.5}{2}(20.8+27.2)+\frac{13.5}{2}(27.2+29.2)\\ &\approx 324+380.7\\ &\approx 704.7\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$

To the nearest square metre, the two-application estimate is $705\text{ m}^2$.

Solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue; diagrams use black ordinary ink and semantic red chords. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged. Final-size rendering and independent source/mathematical review remain subsequent stages.

examples.derivation: A ≈ (20/2)(24+36) = 600 m². Both Bézier control points lie above the endpoint chord, so the curve lies above that chord throughout the interior. The trapezium omits area and underestimates. This adapts the source's single-application example and boundary-comparison follow-up.

One application: (27/2)(20.8+29.2) = 675 m². Two applications use h = 27/2 = 13.5 m: A₁ ≈ 6.75(48) = 324 m² and A₂ ≈ 6.75(56.4) = 380.7 m². Total ≈ 704.7 m², rounding to 705 m². The diagram places the middle offset halfway along the labelled total baseline. The source demonstrates successive one- and two-application estimates for the same region.

A₁ ≈ (14/2)(30+18) = 336 m²; A₂ ≈ (14/2)(18+28) = 322 m²; total ≈ 658 m². In strip 1, both Bézier control points lie below its chord, giving an overestimate. In strip 2, both lie above its chord, giving an underestimate. The solution chords connect the correct offset endpoints. This combines the source's two-strip calculation with its geometric comparison method.
